subject.title: Heartbeat skipped reason 'target-none' is misleading when delivery is disabled by default

question: Should OpenClaw keep `target-none` as the machine-readable heartbeat skip reason and add an additive disabled-delivery hint, or rename the reason string itself?
rationale: Both approaches reduce operator confusion, but the rename has compatibility risk while the additive hint creates a small new diagnostic payload surface.

options.title: Add hint, keep reason
options.body: Keep `reason: "target-none"` stable and surface a human-readable disabled-delivery hint in heartbeat events/status output.

options.title: Rename reason
options.body: Change the machine reason to a clearer value such as `delivery-disabled`, accepting potential parser/log compatibility churn.

options.title: Document only
options.body: Leave runtime output unchanged and rely on docs/troubleshooting text, which avoids API churn but leaves the confusing CLI/log signal in place.

recommendation.title: Add hint, keep reason
recommendation.body: Keep `reason: "target-none"` stable and surface a human-readable disabled-delivery hint in heartbeat events/status output.

likelyOwner.reason: The default-disabled heartbeat behavior traces to the merged heartbeat-default work and this is now a compatibility/product choice for that diagnostic contract.
